answers.explanation: 1969 first nodes, 1974 Cerf and Kahn's paper, 1977 the three-network demonstration, 1983 flag day.
UCLA, SRI, UCSB, and Utah, in 1969. RFC 1 is from the same year.
Their 1974 paper described carrying data across different networks joined by gateways.
RFC 1: 1969. Three-network demonstration: 1977. DoD adoption: 1982. ARPANET shut down: 1990.
The DoD adopted it in 1982. Flag day was January 1, 1983.
ARPANET shut down in 1990. The IPv4 pool ran out in 2011, two decades later.
AUTODIN (1960s), ARPANET (1969), flag day (1983), IPv6 (designed in the 1990s).
Postel edited the RFCs, Crocker wrote RFC 1, Cerf co-designed TCP/IP with Kahn, and BBN built the IMPs.
